chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from one who narrated it, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

I asked him about a man who is afflicted with janabah on a cold night and fears for his life if he performs ghusl. He said: He performs tayammum, and when he is safe from the cold, he performs ghusl and repeats the salat.

key_terms.اغْتَسَلَ: he performs ghusl, the ritual bath
key_terms.التَّلَفَ: destruction or serious harm feared for oneself
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the ritual prayer that is to be repeated here
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.لَيْلَةٍ بَارِدَةٍ: a cold night causing hardship in the use of water
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum as a substitute for purification with water

ai.seo_question: What should a person in janabah do if cold weather makes ghusl dangerous?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person in janabah who fears harm from using water in severe cold. He should perform tayammum in place of ghusl, and when the danger from the cold has passed, he should perform ghusl and repeat the salat.
